601.fixup: conflicts with disk tier, NVFP4 TP and FTW validation combined; the unified-memory warning follows our hit-D2D default

Own version gates on NVIDIA and >=512 out features, makes it opt-out with linear.none=torch, requires a row-major weight, uses ValueError checks, and covers the tied head.
585.summary: Runs a single-row bf16 projection as one GEMV, a decode bs=1 bandwidth win
585.fixup: NVIDIA-only, >=512 out features, opt-out via linear.none=torch, covers the tied LM head

334.title: fix(memory): honor cgroup memory limits when sizing expert banks
334.reason: Right goal (containers were OOM-killed mid-load because the loader sized against the host's MemAvailable). The PR's 294-line module charges memory.current in full, which counts page cache: a container that just read its checkpoint reads as full. Own ~90-line version clamps MemAvailable to the tightest cgroup v2/v1 limit and counts inactive_file as free; used by the expert-bank loader, ft bench bw and the load bench.
334.summary: Loader sized expert banks against host MemAvailable, so containers were OOM-killed; cgroup limits now honored
334.fixup: ~90-line version: clamps to the tightest cgroup v2/v1 limit and counts inactive_file as free

233.title: fix(engine): probe the real WSL pin budget instead of guessing 40% RAM
233.reason: Right goal (WSL refuses pinning far below the 40%-of-RAM guess, so loads died in cudaHostRegister). The PR probes at most 8 GiB (capping large hosts at 6.4 GiB), returns None = uncapped when nothing pins, and predates main's reserved-bytes signature. Own version probes up to the old estimate via the pinned extension (which clears the latched error, #144), returns 0 when nothing pins, and is cached.
233.summary: WSL refuses pinning well below the 40%-of-RAM guess, so loads died; the pin budget is now probed
233.fixup: Probes up to the old estimate via the pinned extension, returns 0 when nothing pins, cached

144.title: fix(kernel): clear the latched CUDA error before raising in pinned_tensor
144.reason: A refused pin (low RAM) left the CUDA error latched, so the next unrelated CUDA call failed as if it were its own -- it breaks exactly the fallback paths a low-RAM load relies on. Clean, HIP mappings already exist.
144.summary: A refused pin left the CUDA error latched, breaking the next unrelated CUDA call; the error is now cleared before raising

56.title: kernel: clamp zero-size host registrations; WDDM lock-pool hint on pin failure
56.reason: The empty-bank failure is real but now hits earlier: an anonymous mmap of 0 bytes raises EINVAL before host_register, so the PR's clamp no longer helps. Own fix gives an empty bank one block, an empty tensor and device_ptr()=0. The PR's RLIMIT_MEMLOCK hint is dropped (cudaHostRegister is not bound by it); main already has PinFailed + _pin_hint.
56.summary: Empty expert banks failed to allocate; now an empty bank gets one block, an empty tensor and device_ptr()=0
56.fixup: Own fix at the mmap level (0-byte mmap fails before host_register); RLIMIT_MEMLOCK hint dropped

354.title: feat(kvcache): store the KV cache as fp8 e4m3 codes (--kv-cache-dtype fp8)
354.reason: Best of the KV-quant group: e4m3 codes + one fp32 scale per (token, kv head), robust to outliers; covers MHA (incl. GDN hybrid), hybrid-SWA, QSA and MLA/DSA. On the 27B = RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 on the RTX 4090, --max-running-requests 1 --memory-ratio 0.95 --max-prefill-length 2048: KV 13420 -> 26427 tokens, decode 46.2 vs 46.6 tok/s (triton instead of fi), same quality (Q&A, 8k fact retrieval, 15 codes in 7.4k); coherent on Qwen3-0.6B where #126 produced NaN. 354.summary: Adds fp8 e4m3 KV cache (--kv-cache-dtype fp8) with per-token/head scales; roughly doubles KV capacity on the 27B
354.fixup: Test doubles for newer attributes, a one-ulp tolerance on sm_89, docs say MLA/DSA is covered

408.summary: Adds nvfp4 KV cache on top of #354: 3.46x the bf16 KV tokens, opt-in (~15% slower decode at 8k)

495.reason: Real ZMQ slow-joiner race: with tp>1, rank 0 could broadcast before a rank's SUB subscription reached the PUB, dropping the message and hanging both ranks. 466.summary: Masks a likely sender-side race instead of fixing it; partial frames still crash; Windows-only, not reproducible

464.title: fix(scheduler): match stop strings with incremental decoding
464.reason: The scheduler matched stop strings on a window of max_chars+1 tokens decoded on its own, so a stop over multi-token characters (rare CJK, emoji under byte-level BPE) was missed, a half-decoded character could match, and the detokenizer then failed to trim the stop. Now matches against the same incremental decode the detokenizer streams. The PR had no tests; fixup adds five (four fail before). Live on Qwen3-0.6B: CJK stop strings trim correctly, same as before for single-token characters.
464.summary: Stop strings spanning multi-token characters were missed; scheduler now matches the detokenizer's text

315.title: Fix GGUF user-defined token atomicity
315.reason: GGUF user-defined tokens (token_type 4, e.g. <think>) keep their vocab id but transformers' GGUF conversion may not register them, so encode() split them into subwords. They are now re-added as non-special atomic tokens, only when actually split, without changing vocab size. Checked on the Gemma-4 12B GGUF: its 7 user-defined tokens already encode atomically, so nothing changes there; it matters for other GGUF architectures (e.g. once qwen35moe GGUF arrives). Tests pass.
315.summary: GGUF user-defined tokens (e.g. <think>) were split into subwords; now re-added as atomic tokens when needed

258.title: feat(dflash): support dflash
258.reason: Speculative decoding with a DFlash block-diffusion draft. Rebased onto main and extended: the drafts that exist for our 27B are DFlash2 (dynamic convolutions + candidate selector, added after the z-lab reference), and as written the PR gave no speedup on an RTX 4090: verify graphs existed only for the FA3 backend (sm90), the GDN verify states (144 MiB each on the 27B) ran out of memory, the draft was loaded after the KV pool, every request leaked its KV pages (the integrity check had been switched off for it), each cycle ran two target forwards, and the PR forced the naive cache. With our work: Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 decodes 190-200 tok/s on code/math and ~115 on prose vs 45, greedy output equal up to bf16 ties; prefix reuse stays on (a windowed draft context carried over between chat turns); the GDN commit replays the recurrence instead of storing a state per token, so the context is 64k tokens (naive cache) or 32k (radix) instead of 27k; logprobs per emitted token. On the Qwen3.6 MoE with expert offload the verify graphs now run too: code/math decode ~290-300 tok/s vs 140-150. The adaptive gate times real plain decode steps and switches speculation off per request where the draft loses (German prose here). Several decoding requests speculate together (batched draft and one batched verify graph): four concurrent prompts on the 27B decode ~240 tok/s in total instead of ~123 one at a time; an offloaded MoE keeps one request per verify, where batching would stream more experts.
258.summary: Speculative decoding with DFlash drafts; with our DFlash2 support and fixes the 27B decodes 2.5-4.4x faster (and batches concurrent requests), the offloaded Qwen3.6 MoE ~2x on code and math
258.fixup: DFlash2 drafts and an fp8 draft option; triton and FlashInfer verify graphs (fp8 and bf16 KV); the per-request KV page leak fixed and the integrity check back on; one target forward per cycle instead of two; prefix reuse with a windowed draft context; the GDN commit replays the recurrence (no per-token verify states); verify graphs for an offloaded MoE; a gate that measures plain decode; logprobs on multi-token steps; ft info prices draft, context and verify buffers; batched speculation for several decoding requests
